source_text: Ἠγνόει γὰρ, ὅτι περιπεσεῖται θεότητι, προσδραμὼν ἀνθρωπότητι. Τί οὖν θαυμαστὸν, εἰ καὶ διὰ Κυπριανοῦ πειρᾶται τῆς ἁγίας ψυχῆς, καὶ τοῦ ἀνεπάφου σώματος; Ιʹ. Πλὴν ὁ μὲν ἐπείρα, καὶ προαγωγῷ χρῆται, οὐ γυναίῳ τινὶ παλαιῷ τῶν πρὸς ταῦτα ἐπιτηδείων, ἀλλὰ δαιμόνων τινὶ τῶν φιλοσωμάτων καὶ φιληδόνων· ἐπειδὴ ταχεῖαι πρὸς τὴν τῶν τοιούτων ὑπηρεσίαν αἱ ἀποστατικαὶ δυνάμεις καὶ φθονεραὶ, πολλοὺς κοινωνοὺς ζητοῦσαι τοῦ πτώματος. Καὶ ὁ μισθὸς τῆς προαγωγίας, θυσίαι τε καὶ σπονδαὶ, καὶ ἡ δι' αἱμάτων καὶ κνίσσης οἰκείωσις· τοιούτους γὰρ ἔδει μισθοὺς εἶναι τοῖς τὰ τοιαῦτα χαριζομένοις. Ἡ δὲ ὡς ᾔσθετο τοῦ κακοῦ, καὶ τὴν ἐπιβουλὴν ἔγνω (τα χύτεραι γὰρ αἱ καθαραὶ ψυχαὶ καὶ θεοειδεῖς πρὸς θήραν τοῦ ἐνεργοῦντος, κἂν ὅτι μάλιστα σοφιστικὸς ᾖ καὶ ποικίλος τὴν ἐπιχείρησιν), τί ποιεῖ, καὶ τί ἀντιτεχνᾶται τῷ δημιουργῷ τῆς κακίας; Πάντων ἀπογνοῦσα τῶν ἄλλων, ἐπὶ τὸν Θεὸν καταφεύγει, καὶ προστάτην ποιεῖται κατὰ τοῦ μισητοῦ πόθου τὸν ἑαυτῆς νυμφίον, ὃς καὶ Σωσάνναν ἐῤῥύσατο, καὶ Θέκλαν διέσωσεν· τὴν μὲν ἀπὸ πικρῶν πρεσβυτέρων, τὴν δὲ ἀπὸ τυράννου μνηστῆρος, καὶ τυ ραννικωτέρας μητρός. Τίνα τοῦτον; Χριστὸν, ὃς καὶ πνεύμασιν ἐπιτιμᾷ, καὶ κουφίζει βαπτιζομέ νους, καὶ πεζεύει πέλαγος, καὶ λεγεῶνα πνευμάτων τῷ βυθῷ δίδωσι· καὶ ῥύεται μὲν ἐκ λάκκου δίκαιον λέουσι προτεθέντα βορὰν, καὶ χειρῶν ἐκτάσει τοὺς θῆρας νικήσαντα· ῥύεται δὲ ὑπὸ κήτους καταποθέντα φυγάδα προφήτην, κἀντοῖς σπλάγχνοις τὴν πίστιν διασωσάμενον· σώζει δὲ Ἀσσυρίους ἐν φλογὶ παῖδας, ἀγγέλῳ τὴν πυρὰν καταψύξας, καὶ τοῖς τρισὶ παραζεύξας τὸν τέταρτον. ΙΑʹ. Ταῦτα καὶ πλείω τούτων ἐπιφημίζουσα, καὶ τὴν Παρθένον Μαρίαν ἱκετεύουσα βοηθῆσαι παρθένῳ κινδυνευούσῃ, τὸ τῆς νηστείας καὶ χαμευνίας προβάλλεται φάρμακον· ὁμοῦ μὲν τὸ κάλλος μαραίνουσα ὡς ἐπίβουλον, ἵν' ὑποσπάσῃ τῆς φλογὸς τὴν ὕλην, καὶ δαπανήσῃ τὸ τῶν παθῶν ὑπέκκαυμα· ὁμοῦ δὲ τὸν Θεὸν ἱλεουμένη διὰ τῆς πίστεως καὶ διὰ τῆς ταπεινώσεως· οὐδενὶ γὰρ οὕτω τῶν πάντων, ὡς κακοπαθείᾳ, θεραπεύεται Θεὸς, καὶ δάκρυσι τὸ φιλάνθρωπον ἀντιδίδοται. Ποθεῖτε τὰ ἑξῆς, οἶδ' ὅτι, τοῦ διηγήματος. Ἀγωνιᾶτε γὰρ ὑπὲρ τῆς παρ θένου, καὶ τοῦ ἐραστοῦ δὲ οὐχ ἧττον, μὴ εἰς κακὸν ἀμφοτέροις ὁ πόθος ἔληξεν. Ἀλλὰ θαρσεῖτε. Πίστεως γὰρ ὁ πόθος πρόξενος γίνεται· καὶ παρθένον ἑαυτῷ μνηστεύων ὁ ἐραστὴς, ὑπὸ Χριστοῦ μνηστεύεται· καὶ ἡ μὲν τῶν πόθων φλὸξ ἀποσβέννυται, ἡ δὲ τῆς ἀληθείας ἀνάπτεται. Πῶς καὶ τίνα τρόπον; Ἐν ταῦθά μοι τὸ τοῦ διηγήματος ἥδιστον. Νικᾷ ἡ παρθένος, νικᾶται ὁ δαίμων. Ὁ πειραστὴς πρόσεισι τῷ ἐραστῇ, καταμηνύει τὴν ἧτταν· περιφρονεῖται. Δυσχεραίνει τῆς ὑπεροψίας· ἀμύνεται τὸν ὑπερόπτην. Ἡ ἄμυνα δὲ τίς; Εἰς αὐτὸν εἰσοικίζεται· τὸν τέως θεραπευτὴν, ἵνα κακῷ τὸ κακὸν ἐκκρουσθῇ, καὶ λύσσα λύσσης ἴαμα γένηται. Τῆς παρθένου μὲν ἀποκρούεται, καθάπερ τι μηχάνημα τείχους ὀχυροῦ καὶ γενναίου, λόγου φυγὰς καὶ δεήσεως· τῷ πέμψαντι δὲ προσπαλαίει, (ὢ τοῦ θαύματος!) πρὸς τὸν βαλόντα πάλιν ἀναστραφεὶς, καὶ συμπνίγων, ὥσπερ τινὰ Σαοὺλ δεύτερον. ΙΒʹ. Τί οὖν ὁ ἄφρων ἐραστὴς καὶ σώφρων ἐπίληπτος; Ζητεῖ τοῦ κακοῦ τὴν λύσιν, εὑρίσκει· εὐμή χανον γὰρ ἅπαν τὸ πιεζόμενον.
thought_title: The virgin conquers and the demon turns on Cyprian
orientation: Gregory is recounting how Cyprian sent a demon to seduce the Christian virgin and how she resisted by fleeing to God.
pass_a_gloss: For he did not know that, having run at humanity, he will fall in with divinity. What then is wonderful, if also through Cyprian he makes trial of the holy soul and of the untouched body. But he made the attempt, and he uses as procurer not some old woman, one of those practiced toward such things, but one of the demons, of those that love bodies and love pleasures; since the rebellious powers are swift toward service of such things and envious, seeking many sharers of the fall. And the pay for the procuring was sacrifices and drink offerings and the bonding through blood and fat smoke; for such pays had to be for those granting such favors. But she, when she perceived the evil and knew the plot, for the pure souls and those formed like God are swifter toward hunting of the one at work, even if he be most cunning and varied in the undertaking, what does she do and what art does she use in return against the maker of evil. Having despaired of all other things, she flees to God, and she makes her own bridegroom a protector against the hated desire, who also rescued Susanna and preserved Thecla; the one from bitter elders, the other from a tyrant suitor and a mother still more tyrant. Who is this. Christ, who also rebukes spirits and lightens those being baptized and walks the sea on foot and gives a legion of spirits to the deep; and he rescues a just man cast from a pit as food set before lions and having conquered the beasts by stretching out of hands; and he rescues a fugitive prophet swallowed under a sea monster and having kept faith safe even in the inward parts; and he saves Assyrian youths in flame, having cooled the pyre with an angel and having yoked the fourth beside the three. Uttering these things and more than these as acclamations, and begging the Virgin Mary to aid a virgin in danger, she puts forward as drug the fasting and sleeping on the ground; at once withering her beauty as plotting against her, so that she may draw away matter from the flame and spend the fuel of the passions; and at once appeasing God through faith and through lowliness; for by nothing of all things so as by suffering hardship is God tended, and his love for man is repaid in return by tears. You desire what comes next of the narrative, I know it. For you are in anguish for the virgin, and for the lover no less, lest the desire ended in evil for both. But take courage. For the desire becomes a procurer of faith; and the lover, betrothing a virgin to himself, is betrothed by Christ; and the flame of the desires is quenched, and that of the truth is kindled. How and in what manner. Here for me is the sweetest part of the narrative. The virgin conquers, the demon is conquered. The tempter comes to the lover, reports the defeat; he is despised. He is vexed at the disdain; he avenges himself on the disdainer. And what is the vengeance. He settles in residence into him himself, the former worshiper, so that evil may be driven out by evil and madness may become cure of madness. He is driven off from the virgin, as a device from a strong and noble wall, being flight of word and prayer; but he wrestles against the one who sent him, O the wonder, having turned back again against the one who threw him and throttling him, as a second Saul. What then does the foolish lover and self controlled seized man do. He seeks the release from the evil, he finds it; for all that is pressed is full of resource.

choices.why: means one who leads another on for seduction, fitting a demon sent to seduce
names fallen spirits as powers in revolt, not ordinary demons

choices.term: ἡ δι αἱμάτων καὶ κνίσσης οἰκείωσις
choices.english: bonding through blood and fat smoke
choices.why: oikeiosis is becoming kin, the pay binds Cyprian to demons by sacrifice
sophron is sound in mind and self controlled, not chaste; epileptos is seized and attacked, not afflicted

pass_b_english: He did not know that in rushing at humanity he would run straight into divinity. So what wonder if through Cyprian too he makes trial of a holy soul and an untouched body? Cyprian made the attempt, and for his procurer he took no practiced old woman skilled in such business, but one of the demons that love bodies and love pleasure. For the rebellious powers are swift to serve such ends, and envious, since they seek many companions in their fall. And the pay for this procuring was sacrifices and drink offerings, and bonding through blood and fat smoke. Such had to be the wages for those who grant such favors.

But as soon as she sensed the evil and recognized the plot — for pure souls shaped toward God are quicker to scent the one at work, however crafty and varied his attack — what does she do, and what art does she turn back against the craftsman of evil? Giving up all other hope, she flees to God, and against this hateful lust she makes her own bridegroom her protector, the one who rescued Susanna and saved Thecla, the one from cruel elders and the other from a tyrannical suitor and a still more tyrannical mother. Who is he? Christ, who rebukes spirits, and lifts the baptized, and walks upon the sea, and consigns a legion of spirits to the deep. He rescues from the pit the righteous man thrown to the lions as prey, who overcame the beasts by the stretching out of his hands (Daniel 6:22). He rescues the runaway prophet swallowed by the great fish, who kept his faith even in its belly (Jonah 1:17). He saves the young Assyrians in the flame, cooling the fire with an angel and joining a fourth to the three (Daniel 3:25).

Crying aloud these deeds and still more, and begging Mary the Virgin to aid a virgin in danger, she puts forward the remedy of fasting and sleeping on the ground. At once she withers her beauty as a traitor, to draw the fuel away from the flame and burn up the tinder of the passions. At once she wins over God through faith and through humility. For among all things God is served by nothing as by hardship willingly borne, and His love for mankind is answered with tears.

I know you long for what comes next in the story. For you are anxious for the virgin, and no less for her lover, lest desire end in ruin for them both. But take heart. For desire becomes the occasion of faith. And the lover, while wooing a virgin for himself, is himself wooed by Christ. And the flame of lust is quenched, while the flame of truth is kindled.

How, and in what way? Here for me is the sweetest part of the story. The virgin wins, the demon is defeated. The tempter comes to her lover and reports his defeat. He is treated with scorn. He resents the scorn and takes vengeance on the man who scorned him. And what is the vengeance? He settles and dwells inside Cyprian himself, his former worshiper, so that evil may be driven out by evil, and frenzy become the cure of frenzy. From the virgin he is driven back, as a siege-engine from a strong and noble wall, fleeing before word and prayer. But he grapples with the one who sent him — O the wonder! — turned back against the one who threw him, and throttling him like a second Saul.
What then does the foolish lover do, a self-controlled man now seized? He seeks release from the evil, and he finds it. For everyone under pressure becomes resourceful.
notes: printed spacing damage: τα χύτεραι for ταχύτεραι, τυ ραννικωτέρας for τυραννικωτέρας, βαπτιζομέ νους for βαπτιζομένους, παρ θένου for παρθένου; read as single words
source has section marks Ι, ΙΑ, ΙΒ; gloss follows clause order without adding text

problems.quote: From the virgin he is driven back, as from an engine upon a strong and noble wall, by her flight to word and prayer.
problems.source_quote: Τῆς παρθένου μὲν ἀποκρούεται, καθάπερ τι μηχάνημα τείχους ὀχυροῦ καὶ γενναίου, λόγου φυγὰς καὶ δεήσεως
problems.why: The demon is the engine beaten off the wall (the virgin), and he is the fugitive before word and prayer.
problems.fix: He is beaten back from the virgin as a siege-engine from a strong and noble wall, fleeing before word and prayer.
problems.ruling: Source: the demon (subject of ἀποκρούεται) is repelled from the virgin like a μηχάνημα from a wall; "λόγου φυγὰς καὶ δεήσεως" = fugitive from word and prayer, not her flight. English misattributes the flight to her.

edits.old: From the virgin he is driven back, as from an engine upon a strong and noble wall, by her flight to word and prayer.
edits.new: From the virgin he is driven back, as a siege-engine from a strong and noble wall, fleeing before word and prayer.

fixed: Real mistranslation fixed: source has μηχάνημα as the demon himself repelled from the wall (the virgin) and λόγου φυγὰς as the demon a fugitive before word and prayer, not her flight.

last_rejected.quote: cooling the fire with an angel and joining a fourth to the three (Daniel 3:25)
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀγγέλῳ τὴν πυρὰν καταψύξας, καὶ τοῖς τρισὶ παραζεύξας τὸν τέταρτον
last_rejected.why: Daniel 3:25 is only the fourth figure. The angel who cools the furnace is LXX Daniel 3:49–50; an angel is also named at 3:28.
last_rejected.fix: cooling the fire by an angel (LXX Daniel 3:49–50) and joining a fourth to the three (Daniel 3:25).
last_rejected.ruling: The translator cited Daniel 3:25 for the fourth figure (τὸν τέταρτον); the citation is a reasonable anchor for the passage, and the angel cooling the fire appears in the Greek additions, so no meaning is changed.

last_rejected.quote: who overcame the beasts by the stretching out of his hands (Daniel 6:22)
last_rejected.why: Daniel 6:22 says an angel shut the lions’ mouths because of Daniel’s innocence, not that outstretched hands overcame them.
last_rejected.fix: who overcame the beasts by stretching out his hands — cite Daniel 6:22 only for the rescue from the den.
last_rejected.ruling: Daniel 6 is the general lions' den reference for the passage (λέουσι προτεθέντα βορὰν). The source's χειρῶν ἐκτάσει is rendered faithfully. The cited verse is a loose anchor, not a changed meaning.

last_rejected.quote: who kept his faith even in its belly (Jonah 1:17)
last_rejected.source_quote: κἀν τοῖς σπλάγχνοις τὴν πίστιν διασωσάμενον
last_rejected.why: Jonah 1:17 tells only of the swallowing. Keeping faith inside the fish is the prayer in Jonah 2.
last_rejected.fix: who kept his faith even in its belly (Jonah 2:1–9).
last_rejected.ruling: Jonah 1:17 anchors the swallowing by the great fish (κήτους καταποθέντα). Keeping faith in its belly (σπλάγχνοις) is rendered faithfully. The loose reference does not change the meaning.
